mitra-cafe.blurb: A Shobhabazar cabin that has been serving since 1920, started by Sushil Roy with one cook and a helper and named for his friend Ganesh Mitra.

tips.expect: A cabin-style eatery with a short menu of fries, cutlets and pudding, in the middle of North Kolkata.
tips.good: The fish kabiraji and the old-fashioned chocolate pudding.
tips.watch: It is small and gets very busy on Puja evenings.
tips.tip: A natural stop after the Shobhabazar Rajbaris and before Nobin Chandra Das.

kolkata-rajbari.blurb: A Bengali restaurant at 56 Jatin Das Road, Lake Terrace, open from about noon to 11 pm.

tips.expect: A traditional Bengali menu in a Rajbari-style setting. About ₹1,200 for two.
tips.good: Mutton kosha is the most-mentioned dish.
tips.watch: Reviews are mixed (around 3.2 stars), so go for the classic dishes rather than experimenting.
tips.tip: Handy near the Lake Market cafes and Deshapriya Park.

aaheli-esplanade.blurb: Aaheli at the Peerless Inn on Chowringhee, opened in 1993 as the city's first authentic Bengali restaurant in a hotel.

tips.expect: A calm, elegant Bengali meal. Lunch is 12:30 to 3 pm and dinner 7:30 to 11 pm.
tips.good: The thali, and special-occasion dishes like the smoked hilsa.
tips.watch: Two fixed sittings, so you can't walk in at 4 pm.
tips.tip: Book for dinner on Ashtami or Navami. It is a minute from Esplanade metro.

aaheli-lake-market.blurb: Aaheli's Lake Market outlet on Sarat Bose Road, from the same Peerless Bengali restaurant brand.

tips.expect: The same Bengali menu style as the Esplanade original, including the Aaheli thali.
tips.good: A good sit-down Bengali meal near the Kalighat pandal circuit.
tips.watch: This is a different outlet from the Peerless Inn original, so check its timings separately.

sonargaon.blurb: The Indian restaurant of the Taj Bengal hotel. The menu leans Punjabi, with Bengali items and special Bengali thalis.

tips.expect: Hotel fine dining in an elegant room.
tips.good: The Bengali thalis it runs seasonally.
tips.watch: Expensive compared with the rest of this list.
tips.tip: Book ahead and check for Puja-special menus.

kareem-s.blurb: The Sector V outlet of the Mughlai name, in Srijan Corporate Park, open noon to 11 pm daily.

tips.expect: A smart Mughlai and North Indian room in an office park.
tips.good: Bheja fry and tawa pulao come up most in reviews.
tips.watch: It is a modern mall-style outlet, not the old Zakaria Street original.
tips.tip: Convenient after the Salt Lake pandals.

oudh-1590-saltlake.blurb: A Nawabi-style dining room in Sector 1, Salt Lake, serving dum-cooked Awadhi and Mughlai dishes. The chain's first outlet opened in 2013 at Deshapriya Park.

tips.expect: Awadhi decor and slow-cooked dum food.
tips.tip: There are other Oudh outlets in the city if Salt Lake is full.

trincas-restaurant-and-bar.blurb: Opened in 1927 as a Swiss tearoom by Cinzio Trinca and his wife, and from 1959 a nightclub and live-music venue where Usha Uthup spent a decade.
dishes: Live music sessions through the day

tips.expect: A Park Street legend where dining and live music go together, with several sessions a day.
tips.good: The music and the nostalgia. Jazz has a long history here.
tips.watch: Seats near the stage fill quickly in the evening.
tips.tip: It is directly opposite Flurys at 17 Park Street. A good pairing for breakfast, then dinner.

pancham-er-adday.blurb: A nostalgic RD Burman-themed cafe at 62/3 Hindustan Park, with an affordable menu.

tips.expect: A tiny, themed adda cafe with R.D. Burman memorabilia.
tips.good: The theme and the low prices.
tips.watch: It is small, so it fills quickly.
tips.tip: Right by the Hindustan Park pandal, so an easy coffee stop.

abar-baithak-the-coffee-shop.blurb: Said to be the first cafe to open in Jodhpur Park. It has two floors, a Feluda theme, and sells books and quirky mugs, bags and cushions.

tips.expect: A bookish, themed cafe with Satyajit Ray's detective Feluda as the muse.
tips.good: The Feluda theme and the books on sale.
tips.watch: It is out in Jodhpur Park, on the Jadavpur side.
tips.tip: A calm break during the Jadavpur and Naktala pandals.

dishes: Bijoli Grill fish roll (bhetki and shrimp, crumbed and fried)

tips.expect: A Bengali grill known for its fish dishes.
tips.watch: I found only limited information, and this pin shares a building with other restaurants on Southern Avenue.

arun-tea-stall.blurb: A famous tea stall at 4/1 Sambhunath Pandit Street, near Goal Mandir, Elgin. It is known for saffron tea.

tips.expect: A busy corner stall, open about 7 am to 11:30 pm.
tips.good: The saffron chai with a crisp kachori or samosa.
tips.watch: Standing room only at peak times.
tips.tip: A cheap pause between Elgin Road and Bhowanipore stops.

hard-rock-cafe.blurb: Hard Rock Cafe Kolkata, inside the 103-year-old Park Mansion at 57-A Park Street, with rock memorabilia on the walls.

tips.expect: A lively themed restaurant and bar in a heritage building.
tips.good: The memorabilia and the setting on Park Street.
tips.watch: Weekends and Puja nights are busy and loud.
tips.tip: Good for a big group that can't agree on food.

the-gazeboo.blurb: A Park Street area all-day diner with North Indian, Middle Eastern and Mughlai dishes.

tips.expect: A casual all-day restaurant. About ₹1,200 for two.
tips.watch: Seating can be tight at peak hours.
tips.tip: A practical stop in the Park Street area.

tips.expect: An Italian restaurant and pizzeria at 18-A Park Street, ground floor.
tips.watch: Park Street can be hard to get a table on Puja weekends.
tips.tip: Combine with Flurys and Trincas on the same stretch.
